sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: That I should be the leader of this new Senate majority is an awesome responsibility.
sentences.zh: 我能成为参议院多数党领袖，这是一项艰巨的责任。

sentences.en: As Democrats and Republicans in the Senate haggle over how to share power.
sentences.zh: 随着参议院民主党人和共和党人就如何分享权力进行讨价还价。

sentences.en: We have no choice but to try to work together.
sentences.zh: 我们别无选择，只能尝试合作。

sentences.en: In a chamber split 50 to 50.
sentences.zh: 在一个 50 对 50 分裂的议院中。

sentences.en: So let us begin.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: The Republican leader, Mitch McConnell, made one unconditional demand.
sentences.zh: 共和党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔提出了一个无条件的诉求。

sentences.en: If the talk of unity and common ground is to have meaning.
sentences.zh: 如果关于团结和共同点的谈话要有意义的话。

sentences.en: Do not touch the filibuster rule.
sentences.zh: 不要触碰“冗长辩论”规则。

sentences.en: Then I cannot imagine the Democratic leader would rather hold up the power-sharing agreement than simply reaffirm that his side won't be breaking this standing rule of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 那么我无法想象民主党领袖宁愿搁置权力分享协议，也不愿简单地重申他的一方不会打破这项参议院的现行规则。

sentences.en: A rule that many Democrats believe must be destroyed to get anything big done in the Biden era.
sentences.zh: 许多民主党人认为，为了在拜登时代完成任何大事，必须废除这项规则。

sentences.en: And many Republicans believe must be saved to block the Biden agenda.
sentences.zh: 而许多共和党人则认为，为了阻止拜登的议程，必须保留这项规则。

sentences.en: My colleague, Julie Davis, on the coming battle over the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 我的同事朱莉·戴维斯，关于即将到来的“冗长辩论”之争。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, January 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月28日，星期四。

sentences.en: So Julie, help us understand the filibuster rule, which I think a lot of people think they understand, but they really don't.
sentences.zh: 那么朱莉，帮我们了解一下“冗长辩论”规则，我想很多人以为自己了解，但其实并不了解。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So most people, when they hear filibuster, they think of someone talking on and on as a way to delay something in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 大多数人在听到“冗长辩论”时，会想到有人在参议院喋喋不休地说话，以此来拖延某事。

sentences.en: And that's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That is a filibuster.
sentences.zh: 那确实是一种“冗长辩论”。

sentences.en: Then there's the filibuster rule.
sentences.zh: 然后还有“冗长辩论”规则。

sentences.en: This is the thing that's being debated in the Senate right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是参议院目前正在辩论的事情。

sentences.en: And it is the mechanism for stopping a senator from going on and on and on and allowing the Senate to move to a vote.
sentences.zh: 它是阻止参议员没完没了地发言，并允许参议院进行投票的机制。

sentences.en: And in its current form, it requires 60 votes to do that.
sentences.zh: 按照目前的规定，需要60票才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: So you need to be able to get three fifths of the Senate to agree that we're going to stop talking about this and move on to a vote or move on to consider something before you can do it.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要获得参议院五分之三的同意，才能停止讨论并进入投票，或者在进行投票前考虑其他事项。

sentences.en: So that's its main effect.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的主要作用。

sentences.en: And in a lot of ways, it is kind of the ultimate expression of what the Senate is about.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，它算是参议院本质的终极体现。

sentences.en: The Senate operates on consensus.
sentences.zh: 参议院以共识为基础运作。

sentences.en: It's not enough to just have a majority plus one.
sentences.zh: 仅仅拥有多数加一票是不够的。

sentences.en: And that is kind of the nature of the Senate as opposed to the House.
sentences.zh: 这与众议院不同，是参议院的本质所在。

sentences.en: It is supposed to be, they call it the cooling saucer,
sentences.zh: 它本应是所谓的“冷却碟”，

sentences.en: where members are taking more time and deliberating more carefully and cutting deals and discussing more thoroughly legislation, rather than the House, where majority rules,
sentences.zh: 议员们在这里花费更多时间，更审慎地审议，达成协议，并更彻底地讨论立法，而不像众议院那样多数派说了算，

sentences.en: the minority really can't stop anything.
sentences.zh: 少数派真的无法阻止任何事情。

sentences.en: And whatever 50% of the members want to do, that's what happens.
sentences.zh: 只要50%的成员想做什么，事情就会发生。

sentences.en: The Senate has always prided itself on being a very different place that operates in a very different way.
sentences.zh: 参议院一直以自己是一个非常不同的地方、以非常不同的方式运作而自豪。

sentences.en: And the filibuster has become one of the main reasons why.
sentences.zh: 而“冗长辩论”已成为其中主要原因之一。

sentences.en: So it has become really the core of the way the Senate works and, more recently,
sentences.zh: 所以它确实成为了参议院运作方式的核心，而最近，

sentences.en: the way the Senate has become paralyzed because it's really difficult to get the agreement of 60 senators to move forward on pretty much anything.
sentences.zh: 参议院陷入瘫痪，因为要获得60名参议员的同意来推进几乎任何事情都非常困难。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And so at this moment, in this unusual 50-50 split, what it means on a practical level, correct me if I'm wrong, is that Democrats, with their 50 seats,
sentences.zh: 那么在这一刻，在这个不同寻常的50-50分裂局面下，从实际层面来说，如果我没理解错的话，这意味着拥有50个席位的民主党人，

sentences.en: need 10 Republican votes to pretty much do anything.
sentences.zh: 几乎做任何事都需要10张共和党人的选票。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So help me understand the history of the filibuster rule, where it comes from and how it has been used.
sentences.zh: 那么帮我了解一下“冗长辩论”规则的历史，它从何而来，又是如何被使用的。

sentences.en: Well, the filibuster, even though I did say that it sort of is the heart of what the Senate is about, it was not actually an original feature of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，“冗长辩论”虽然我刚才说它是参议院的核心，但它实际上并非参议院最初的特征。

sentences.en: It's not in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 宪法中并没有这一条。

sentences.en: It was a rule that was established in 1917.
sentences.zh: 这是一项在1917年制定的规则。

sentences.en: Initially, it was two-thirds of the Senate, 67 votes to be able to cut off debate and move on.
sentences.zh: 最初，需要参议院三分之二，即67票才能结束辩论并继续进行。

sentences.en: And then it was changed in 1975 to three-fifths, so it's 60 votes.
sentences.zh: 后来在1975年改为五分之三，也就是60票。

sentences.en: And perhaps the most famous example is former Senator Strom Thurmond, the late Senator Strom Thurmond of South Carolina,
sentences.zh: 也许最著名的例子是前参议员斯特罗姆·瑟蒙德，已故的南卡罗来纳州参议员斯特罗姆·瑟蒙德，

sentences.en: using the filibuster in 1957 to stop the civil rights law from going forward.
sentences.zh: 他在1957年利用“冗长辩论”阻止民权法案的推进。

sentences.en: He talked for nearly 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 他讲了近24个小时。

sentences.en: In that case, it was just him on the floor for the entire time.
sentences.zh: 在那次事件中，整个过程中只有他一个人在发言席上。

sentences.en: And he was essentially blocking this major civil rights measure from going forward.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是在阻止这项重大的民权措施向前推进。

sentences.en: And then there was a reprise of that seven years later when Thurmond and several other Southern segregationist senators filibustered the 1964 Civil Rights Act and essentially delayed for a couple of months the Senate's ability to move forward on that.
sentences.zh: 七年后，瑟蒙德和其他几位南方种族隔离主义参议员对1964年的《民权法案》进行了“冗长辩论”，实际上将参议院推进该法案的能力拖延了几个月。

sentences.en: So it has a very long and storied history of being used to really stand in the way of what we think of now as some of the biggest policy initiatives that are at the heart of what this country is.
sentences.zh: 所以它有着非常悠久且传奇的历史，被用来阻碍我们现在认为的、构成这个国家核心的一些最重要的政策倡议。

sentences.en: So this is a very dark use of the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 所以这是“冗长辩论”非常黑暗的一面。

sentences.en: And what these senators were up to was delaying the point at which 60 of their colleagues could vote to actually pass the civil rights legislation, which ultimately did pass.
sentences.zh: 这些参议员所做的是推迟60名同事投票通过民权立法的时刻，尽管该法案最终还是通过了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: At that time, the senators needed 67 votes.
sentences.zh: 当时，参议员们需要67票。

sentences.en: And by getting up and speaking for almost a full day, Thurmond is registering his opposition, not just to the bill itself, but to moving forward on it at all.
sentences.zh: 通过站起来发言近一整天，瑟蒙德不仅表达了他对法案本身的反对，也表达了对推进该法案的反对。

sentences.en: And unless there were 67 senators who agreed to shut him down, he could keep talking and talking.
sentences.zh: 除非有67名参议员同意让他闭嘴，否则他可以一直说下去。

sentences.en: And it has remained through the years a singular mechanism for delaying or blocking legislation and also nominations.
sentences.zh: 多年来，它一直是一种用于拖延或阻止立法以及提名的独特机制。

sentences.en: And it has become more and more a thorn in the side of the majority.
sentences.zh: 它也越来越成为多数派眼中钉。

sentences.en: The Democrats, led by then Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, after many,
sentences.zh: 民主党人，在时任参议院多数党领袖哈里·里德的领导下，在经历了许多、

sentences.en: many months of feuding with Republicans who were refusing to confirm or allow nominations from former President Barack Obama to go forward in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 许多个月与共和党的争斗后，共和党人拒绝确认或允许前总统巴拉克·奥巴马的提名在参议院推进。

sentences.en: Senate Democrats, who then had control of the chamber, decided to take a pretty extreme measure, something that had never happened to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 当时控制议院的参议院民主党人决定采取一项相当极端的措施，这是参议院从未发生过的事情。

sentences.en: The change we propose today would ensure executive and judicial nominations, an up or down vote on confirmation, yes, no.
sentences.zh: 我们今天提出的改变将确保行政和司法提名，进行确认投票，赞成或反对，是或否。

sentences.en: And change the rules so that the filibuster could no longer be used for executive nominations, including judicial nominations.
sentences.zh: 并修改规则，使得“冗长辩论”不再能用于行政提名，包括司法提名。

sentences.en: Today, Democrats and independents are saying enough is enough.
sentences.zh: 今天，民主党人和独立人士说，受够了。

sentences.en: To change the rules regarding presidential nominees will apply equally to both parties.
sentences.zh: 关于总统提名的规则变更将同样适用于两党。

sentences.en: When Republicans are in power, these changes will apply to them just as well.
sentences.zh: 当共和党人掌权时，这些变化同样适用于他们。

sentences.en: That, Mr. President, is simple fairness.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，这就是简单的公平。

sentences.en: And so the Democrats used what's called detonating the nuclear option.
sentences.zh: 于是民主党人使用了所谓的“引爆核选项”。

sentences.en: Wow, that's evocative.
sentences.zh: 哇，这真形象。

sentences.en: It's a procedural bomb.
sentences.zh: 这是一枚程序炸弹。

sentences.en: And the way that it works is, even though it takes 60 votes to move forward with a nomination or legislation, it only takes a majority of the Senate to change the rules.
sentences.zh: 它的运作方式是，尽管推进提名或立法需要60票，但改变规则只需要参议院多数票。

sentences.en: So under the precedent set by the Senate today, November 21st, 2013, the threshold on nominations, not including those to the Supreme Court of the United States, is now a majority.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据参议院今天（2013年11月21日）确立的先例，提名的门槛（不包括美国最高法院的提名）现在是多数票。

sentences.en: That is the ruling of the chair.
sentences.zh: 这就是主席的裁决。

sentences.en: That was it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: That they shaved off a big part of what the filibuster does.
sentences.zh: 他们削减了“冗长辩论”很大一部分功能。

sentences.en: And this change that was made in 2013 was viewed as a pretty extreme thing to do.
sentences.zh: 2013年做出的这一改变被认为是一件相当极端的事情。

sentences.en: The Senate operates, as I said, on consensus.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，参议院以共识为基础运作。

sentences.en: There's a set of rules and precedents that drives everything that gets done.
sentences.zh: 有一套规则和先例驱动着所做的一切。

sentences.en: And this was a very bare-knuckled move on the part of Democrats to say, this rule that we've all been living under for all these many,
sentences.zh: 这是民主党人非常强硬的举动，意思是，我们几十年来一直生活在其中的这条规则，

sentences.en: many decades is simply standing in the way of progress.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是阻碍了进步。

sentences.en: And we're going to use our power as the majority to change it.
sentences.zh: 我们将利用多数派的权力来改变它。

sentences.en: So Democrats changed the filibuster rule just for presidential nominations, specifically for the judiciary.
sentences.zh: 所以民主党人修改了“冗长辩论”规则，仅针对总统提名，特别是司法提名。

sentences.en: And they were able to do that with 51 votes, even though the rule involves 60.
sentences.zh: 他们能够以51票做到这一点，尽管该规则涉及60票。

sentences.en: I don't know how you keep track of all this, Julie.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是怎么跟踪所有这些事情的，朱莉。

sentences.en: Covering the Senate seems like a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 报道参议院听起来像是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: But they were able to do this.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: They were able to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们能够做到。

sentences.en: And let's remember that it was Senate Democrats who pioneered, who literally pioneered.
sentences.zh: 请记住，正是参议院民主党人开创了，他们确实开创了。

sentences.en: The practice of filibustering circuit court nominees.
sentences.zh: 对巡回法院提名人进行“冗长辩论”的做法。

sentences.en: And who've been its biggest proponents in the very recent paSt.
sentences.zh: 并且在最近的过去，他们一直是其最大的支持者。

sentences.en: Republicans warned them at the time that this was wholly inappropriate use of their powers in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在当时警告他们，这是在参议院滥用权力的行为。

sentences.en: And now they want to blow up the rules because Republicans are following a precedent they themselves set.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们想炸毁规则，因为共和党人正在遵循他们自己设定的先例。

sentences.en: That this was doing away with an important rule and an important tool.
sentences.zh: 这是在废除一项重要的规则和重要的工具。

sentences.en: And that when the tables were turned, they were going to have to live with the consequences that they created.
sentences.zh: 当风水轮流转时，他们将不得不承担自己造成的后果。

sentences.en: That they would live to regret this.
sentences.zh: 他们终将为此感到后悔。

sentences.en: Say to my friends on the other side of the aisle, you'll regret this.
sentences.zh: 我对走廊对面的朋友们说，你们会后悔的。

sentences.en: And you may regret it a lot sooner than you think.
sentences.zh: 而且你们后悔的时间可能比你们想象的要早得多。

sentences.en: And do Democrats come to regret this?
sentences.zh: 那么民主党人后来后悔了吗？

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们后悔了。

sentences.en: And it's only four years before they do.
sentences.zh: 而且仅仅四年后他们就后悔了。

sentences.en: Because President Trump wins the election in 2016.
sentences.zh: 因为特朗普总统在2016年赢得了选举。

sentences.en: And in 2017, he has the opportunity to nominate his first Supreme Court nominee, Neil Gorsuch.
sentences.zh: 2017年，他有机会提名他的第一位最高法院大法官人选，尼尔·戈萨奇。

sentences.en: And Democrats quickly say that, you know, they're going to have to look at this very closely.
sentences.zh: 民主党人很快表示，你知道，他们必须非常仔细地审视这一点。

sentences.en: And they may not be willing to move forward with this.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不愿意推进此事。

sentences.en: And there is clearly a threat that they are going to filibuster President Trump's Supreme Court nominee.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们威胁要对特朗普总统的最高法院提名人进行“冗长辩论”。

sentences.en: And Republicans turn around and have their revenge.
sentences.zh: 共和党人转过身来进行了报复。

sentences.en: And they say, what was good for you when you were in majority is good for us.
sentences.zh: 他们说，当你们在多数派时对你们有利的事情，对我们也同样有利。

sentences.en: Now that we're in the majority and potentially facing obstruction of our president's Supreme Court nominee.
sentences.zh: 现在我们是多数派，并且可能面临对我们总统最高法院提名人的阻挠。

sentences.en: And they do the very same thing that Democrats did in 2013.
sentences.zh: 他们做了民主党人在2013年所做的同样的事情。

sentences.en: They detonate the nuclear option and eliminate the last bit of power to filibuster a judicial nominee, making it impossible to do that for a Supreme Court nomination.
sentences.zh: 他们引爆了“核选项”，消除了对司法提名人进行“冗长辩论”的最后一点权力，使得对最高法院提名进行“冗长辩论”变得不可能。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And knowing that they only need 51 votes to put a Trump-appointed Supreme Court justice on the court,
sentences.zh: 并且知道他们只需要51票就能让特朗普任命的最高法院大法官进入法院，

sentences.en: Republicans get those 51 votes for Neil Gorsuch and later for Brett Kavanaugh and for Amy Coney Barrett.
sentences.zh: 共和党人获得了尼尔·戈萨奇的51票，后来又获得了布雷特·卡瓦诺和艾米·科尼·巴雷特的选票。

sentences.en: And it's a classic, be careful what you wish for moment,
sentences.zh: 这是一个经典的“小心你所祈求的”时刻，

sentences.en: because Democrats' decision to end the filibuster rule on judicial nominations below the Supreme Court opens up the chance for Republicans to then end the filibuster rule on Supreme Court nominees.
sentences.zh: 因为民主党人决定结束对最高法院以下司法提名的“冗长辩论”规则，为共和党人随后结束对最高法院提名人的“冗长辩论”规则打开了大门。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It allowed Mitch McConnell to push through a ton of lower court judicial nominees and allowed President Trump to win, with a simple majority,
sentences.zh: 它允许米奇·麦康奈尔强行通过了大量下级法院的司法提名，并允许特朗普总统以简单多数票，

sentences.en: confirmation of three conservative Supreme Court justices.
sentences.zh: 确认了三位保守派最高法院大法官。

sentences.en: So at this point, we see pretty clearly the problems with the filibuster rule.
sentences.zh: 所以此时此刻，我们非常清楚地看到了“冗长辩论”规则的问题。

sentences.en: We can see how it allows the minority to delay and in some cases block essential and just causes like civil rights protections.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到它如何允许少数派拖延，在某些情况下阻碍像民权保护这样重要且正义的事业。

sentences.en: And we can see the problems with eliminating the filibuster rule, how that can haunt the minority when it comes to something like the American judiciary and what it looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以看到取消“冗长辩论”规则的问题，当涉及到美国司法机构及其面貌时，这会如何困扰少数派。

sentences.en: So the filibuster rule is a pretty tricky affair.
sentences.zh: 所以“冗长辩论”规则是一件相当棘手的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like any power worth having, it has its advantages and it has its risks and drawbacks and getting rid of it has its own set of issues.
sentences.zh: 就像任何值得拥有的权力一样，它有其优势，也有其风险和弊端，而摆脱它也有其自身的一系列问题。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what the Senate is grappling with right now.
sentences.zh: 这正是参议院目前正在努力解决的问题。

sentences.en: It is why Mitch McConnell is trying to exact these promises from Democrats that they're not going to get rid of the filibuster rule and why Democrats feel like they really are not in a position at this point to make that promise.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么米奇·麦康奈尔试图从民主党人那里得到这些承诺，即他们不会废除“冗长辩论”规则，也是为什么民主党人觉得他们目前真的无法做出那个承诺。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, Julie, that brings us up to now and these negotiations between Democrats and Republicans over power sharing and the future of the filibuster rule.
sentences.zh: 那么，朱莉，这让我们回到了现在，以及民主党和共和党之间关于权力分享和“冗长辩论”规则未来的谈判。

sentences.en: What is former Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell asking Democrats specifically to commit themselves to doing or not doing when it comes to the filibuster rule?
sentences.zh: 前参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔具体要求民主党人承诺在“冗长辩论”规则方面做什么或不做什么？

sentences.en: McConnell is asking Democrats to promise that they will not do what both he and the former Democratic Majority Leader Harry Reid did and detonate the nuclear option to get rid of what is really the last bit of filibuster power.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔要求民主党人承诺，他们不会做他和前民主党多数党领袖哈里·里德都做过的事情，即引爆“核选项”来废除实际上最后一点“冗长辩论”权力。

sentences.en: There is the power to filibuster legislation.
sentences.zh: 那就是对立法进行“冗长辩论”的权力。

sentences.en: He's asking them to promise up front that they will not get rid of that part of the rule and thus preserve the minority's ability to delay or block legislation for the entirety of their control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他要求他们预先承诺，他们不会废除规则的那一部分，从而在他们控制参议院的整个期间保留少数派拖延或阻止立法的能力。

sentences.en: And what is McConnell's argument to Democrats for keeping it and requiring them to promise publicly that they won't get rid of it?
sentences.zh: 那么麦康奈尔对民主党人提出的保留该规则并要求他们公开承诺不会废除它的论点是什么？

sentences.en: The Senate exists to require deliberation and cooperation.
sentences.zh: 参议院的存在是为了要求审议与合作。

sentences.en: He basically is making the argument that the filibuster is fundamental to what the Senate is.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在论证，阻挠议事是参议院立身之本。

sentences.en: If the Democratic majority were to attack the filibuster, they would guarantee themselves immediate chaos.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党多数派要攻击阻挠议事规则，他们就是在自找即刻的混乱。

sentences.en: And destroying the filibuster would drain comedy and consent from this body to a degree that would be unparalleled in living memory.
sentences.zh: 摧毁阻挠议事规则将使这个机构丧失妥协与共识，其程度在当代记忆中前所未有。

sentences.en: And that eliminating the minority's ability to have its say on legislation would make it a place where the majority rules and legislation is made according to the whims of the moment.
sentences.zh: 而消除少数派在立法上发表意见的能力，将使这里变成一个多数派说了算、立法随一时兴起而制定的地方。

sentences.en: So instead of building stable consensus, we'd be chaotically swapping party platforms,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们不会建立稳定的共识，而是在混乱地交换政党纲领，

sentences.en: swinging wildly between opposite visions that would guarantee half the country is miserable and resentful at any given time.
sentences.zh: 在截然相反的愿景之间剧烈摇摆，这将确保半个国家在任何时候都感到痛苦和怨恨。

sentences.en: And he's also making an appeal to President Biden and the Senate leadership and saying, you all say that you want unity.
sentences.zh: 他同时也在向拜登总统和参议院领导层呼吁，说你们都声称想要团结。

sentences.en: You all say that you want to have bipartisan accomplishments.
sentences.zh: 你们都说想要取得两党合作的成就。

sentences.en: If you really want that, what you need to do is demonstrate that by taking this bare-knuckled tactic off the table and saying that you will never deprive us, the minority,
sentences.zh: 如果你们真的想要那样，你们需要做的是通过放弃这种赤裸裸的战术来证明，并承诺永远不会剥夺我们少数派

sentences.en: of the ability to filibuster legislation.
sentences.zh: 阻挠议事立法的能力。

sentences.en: And therefore, we can all negotiate in good faith going forward.
sentences.zh: 这样，我们今后才能进行真诚的谈判。

sentences.en: Taking that plunge would not be some progressive dream.
sentences.zh: 迈出那一步绝非什么进步派的梦想。

sentences.en: It would be a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 那将是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: I guarantee it.
sentences.zh: 我敢保证。

sentences.en: But to be clear, McConnell has a great deal of self-interest in keeping the filibuster rule.
sentences.zh: 但需要明确的是，麦康奈尔在保留阻挠议事规则上有巨大的自身利益。

sentences.en: He is talking about institutional prerogatives and tradition, but this is also about power.
sentences.zh: 他谈论的是制度特权和传统，但这同时也关乎权力。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell has just had to give up his job as majority leader.
sentences.zh: 米奇·麦康奈尔刚刚不得不放弃他多数党领袖的职位。

sentences.en: He no longer is running the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他不再掌管参议院了。

sentences.en: And the filibuster really is his most powerful tool and the most powerful tool that Republicans have to stop President Biden's agenda,
sentences.zh: 阻挠议事确实是他手中最强大的工具，也是共和党人阻止拜登总统议程的最强工具，

sentences.en: to prevent Democrats from getting done what they want to get done.
sentences.zh: 用以阻止民主党人完成他们想做的事情。

sentences.en: And so, of course, he has a huge interest in exacting a promise, if he can, at the very outset,
sentences.zh: 所以，他当然有巨大的兴趣在最开始时，如果可能的话，强求一个承诺，

sentences.en: that Democrats are not going to essentially neuter Republicans' ability to stop legislation if they oppose it.
sentences.zh: 即民主党人不会从根本上削弱共和党人阻止他们反对的立法的能力。

sentences.en: McConnell's position and this demand he's making to Democrats, it seems to assume that Senate Democrats want to get rid of the filibuster rule.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔的立场和他向民主党人提出的这个要求，似乎假设了参议院民主党人想要废除阻挠议事规则。

sentences.en: Is that actually the case?
sentences.zh: 事实真的如此吗？

sentences.en: Many Senate Democrats have said that they do want to get rid of the filibuster rule, that it's standing in the way of progress,
sentences.zh: 许多参议院民主党人确实说过他们想要废除阻挠议事规则，认为它阻碍了进步，

sentences.en: and that it is time to clear it away and allow big, sweeping legislation that has been bottled up while the Senate was under Republican rule to finally go through.
sentences.zh: 是时候将其清除，让那些在共和党控制参议院期间被搁置的大型、全面的立法最终获得通过了。

sentences.en: Things like tackling climate change, doing something about income inequality, racial justice, the pandemic relief package that everyone's been talking about.
sentences.zh: 比如应对气候变化、解决收入不平等、种族正义，以及大家一直在谈论的疫情纾困方案。

sentences.en: Some of these initiatives are so important, these Democrats would argue, that while they have the power, while they have the numbers in the Senate,
sentences.zh: 这些民主党人会辩称，其中一些倡议非常重要，因此当他们拥有权力，当他们在参议院拥有人数优势时，

sentences.en: they need to push through as much bold policy as they can and use what power they have to do that with the knowledge that they won't be in the majority forever.
sentences.zh: 他们需要尽可能多地推动大胆的政策，并利用他们现有的权力去做这些事，因为他们知道自己不会永远占据多数席位。

sentences.en: In a 50-50 Senate, the likelihood that the Republicans take over in two more years is pretty good, but their idea is, okay,
sentences.zh: 在50对50的参议院中，共和党在两年后接管的可能性很大，但他们的想法是，好吧，

sentences.en: so we just press go and jam a bunch of things through that should have happened a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我们就按下启动键，强行通过一堆早就该发生的事情。

sentences.en: So the argument here from some of these Senate Democrats is, this is our moment, we've got the majority, just do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，一些参议院民主党人的论点是，这是我们的时刻，我们拥有多数席位，那就干吧。

sentences.en: Just get rid of the final remnants of the filibuster rule,
sentences.zh: 干脆废除阻挠议事规则的最后残余，

sentences.en: even though we know from what happened in 2013 that this will someday come back and haunt us because we won't control the Senate forever.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们从2013年发生的事情中知道，这总有一天会回来困扰我们，因为我们不会永远控制参议院。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think there is also, let's call it a hope, that voters would see this, they would see all of these priorities that have languished with no action getting done,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为还有一种希望，姑且称之为希望，即选民会看到这一点，他们会看到所有这些长期搁置、毫无进展的优先事项得以完成，

sentences.en: and that they would actually reward Democrats and, frankly, punish Republicans who tried to stand in the way.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上会奖励民主党人，坦率地说，惩罚那些试图阻挠的共和党人。

sentences.en: So given all of that, what ends up happening in these negotiations between Mitch McConnell and the Democrats?
sentences.zh: 那么考虑到所有这些，米奇·麦康奈尔和民主党人之间的谈判最终会发生什么？

sentences.en: So what ends up happening is Schumer says, no way, I'm not giving you this assurance.
sentences.zh: 最终发生的是舒默说，没门，我不会给你这个保证。

sentences.en: Democrats feel that taking this threat off the table would just be fighting with one arm tied behind their back,
sentences.zh: 民主党人认为，放弃这种威胁就像是自缚双臂进行战斗，

sentences.en: and they're not willing to give up on the possibility that they might one day want to eliminate the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 他们不愿放弃未来某天可能想要废除阻挠议事规则的可能性。

sentences.en: But McConnell backs down because he says that he has gotten assurances from Joe Manchin of West Virginia and Kyrsten Sinema of Arizona,
sentences.zh: 但麦康奈尔退让了，因为他说他从西弗吉尼亚州的乔·曼钦和亚利桑那州的克里斯汀·希内玛那里得到了保证，

sentences.en: two centrist Democrats who have told him and stated publicly that they would never vote with the rest of the Democrats to eliminate the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 这两位中间派民主党人告诉他并公开声明，他们永远不会与其余民主党人一起投票废除阻挠议事规则。

sentences.en: And without their votes, it can't happen.
sentences.zh: 没有他们的投票，这就不可能实现。

sentences.en: So he says with these assurances in hand, he's willing to drop his demand for a formal promise from the majority leader and go forward, organize the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，有了这些保证，他愿意放弃对多数党领袖做出正式承诺的要求，继续前进，组织参议院。

sentences.en: The Democrats can have their committee gavels and everyone can go on their merry way.
sentences.zh: 民主党人可以拿到他们的委员会木槌，大家都可以各行其是了。

sentences.en: Should we consider these assurances from Senators Manchin and Sinema permanent?
sentences.zh: 我们应该认为曼钦和希内玛参议员的这些保证是永久性的吗？

sentences.en: Or should we think of them as many things in the Senate as fungible and temporary and something they might ultimately reverse themselves on?
sentences.zh: 还是我们应该像看待参议院里的许多事情一样，认为它们是可替代且暂时的，是他们最终可能会反悔的事情？

sentences.en: Well, they've been pretty clear of what their views are right now, and they say that they're not changing their minds.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们对自己目前的观点表达得很清楚，他们说他们不会改变主意。

sentences.en: But I think the possibility is still there and is frankly hanging over the Senate and will continue to hang over the Senate that they could change their minds.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这种可能性依然存在，坦率地说，它悬在参议院上空，并将继续悬在参议院上空，即他们可能会改变主意。

sentences.en: If Democrats push forward and find a wall of Republican resistance and filibuster after filibuster after filibuster, they could very well decide that this is untenable.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人继续推进，却发现共和党人筑起了一道阻挠议事又阻挠议事的墙，他们很可能会认为这是站不住脚的。

sentences.en: This is not a way to get anything done, which after all is what they've said they want.
sentences.zh: 这不是完成任何事情的方法，而这毕竟是他们所说的他们想要的。

sentences.en: And already one of the centrists who has been against getting rid of the filibuster, John Tester of Montana, has said that, you know, he has this view now.
sentences.zh: 而且已经有一位一直反对废除阻挠议事规则的中间派，蒙大拿州的约翰·泰斯特，已经表示，你知道，他现在有这种看法。

sentences.en: But if McConnell thinks that he can stand in the way of everything and block action, he may very well have to change his view because his patience isn't infinite.
sentences.zh: 但如果麦康奈尔认为他可以阻碍一切并阻止行动，他很可能不得不改变他的看法，因为他的耐心不是无限的。

sentences.en: Julie, as someone who has covered Congress for a really long time, I'm curious what it tells you that we have gotten to this place where not much of the filibuster rule remains,
sentences.zh: 朱莉，作为一名报道国会很久的人，我很好奇，我们走到这一步，阻挠议事规则所剩无几，这说明了什么，

sentences.en: but the part that remains could go away and be historic, and it would be an enormous change in how the Senate operates.
sentences.zh: 但剩下的部分可能会消失，那将是历史性的，这将是参议院运作方式的巨大改变。

sentences.en: So how are you thinking about that?
sentences.zh: 那么你是怎么看待这个问题的？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, the Senate has become really a den of paralysis in recent years, and it's been frustrating to members of both parties.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，近年来参议院确实成了瘫痪的巢穴，这让两党的成员都感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And I think what this debate is really about is everyone's diagnosed that same problem, and they're just disagreeing over what the cure is.
sentences.zh: 我认为这场辩论的真正焦点是每个人都诊断出了同样的问题，只是在治疗方法上存在分歧。

sentences.en: And it was so interesting back in December, there were two senators, one Republican, one Democrat, retiring, and they both gave their farewell addresses on the floor.
sentences.zh: 去年12月发生的事情非常有趣，有两位参议员，一位共和党人，一位民主党人，即将退休，他们在议事厅发表了告别演说。

sentences.en: Lamar Alexander from Tennessee, the Republican.
sentences.zh: 来自田纳西州的共和党人拉马尔·亚历山大。

sentences.en: Mr. President, I thank my friend Mitch.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，我感谢我的朋友米奇。

sentences.en: Devoted his to saying, you know, this place is so broken, nothing gets done, we really need to rediscover the lost art of legislating.
sentences.zh: 他致力于说，你知道，这个地方太破败了，什么都做不成，我们真的需要重新发现失传的立法艺术。

sentences.en: Lately, the Senate has been like joining the Grand Ole Opry and not being allowed to sing.
sentences.zh: 最近，参议院就像加入了大奥普里剧院却不被允许唱歌一样。

sentences.en: It's a real waste of talent.
sentences.zh: 这真是对人才的浪费。

sentences.en: And how we have to protect the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 以及我们必须如何保护阻挠议事规则。

sentences.en: That eliminating it would destroy the Senate.
sentences.zh: 废除它会摧毁参议院。

sentences.en: Now, some advocate operating the Senate in a different way.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人主张以不同的方式运作参议院。

sentences.en: End the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 结束阻挠议事。

sentences.en: Don't worry about party lines.
sentences.zh: 不要管党派界限。

sentences.en: Pass everything with a majority vote.
sentences.zh: 以多数票通过一切。

sentences.en: He said it would turn into a second House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 他说这会变成第二个众议院。

sentences.en: Ending the filibuster would destroy the impetus for forcing the broad agreements I've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 结束阻挠议事将摧毁推动我所谈论的广泛协议的动力。

sentences.en: And it would unleash the tyranny of the majority to steamroll the rights of the minority.
sentences.zh: 它将释放多数人的暴政，去碾压少数人的权利。

sentences.en: He was very determined to leave the Senate with this message of, you know, don't break down the one tool that still remains to generate consensus in this institution.
sentences.zh: 他非常坚定地带着这个信息离开参议院，即，不要破坏这个机构中仍然存在的唯一能产生共识的工具。

sentences.en: And then Tom Udall from New Mexico, a Democrat, came along a couple days later and gave his farewell speech and said all the same things about how broken this institution was.
sentences.zh: 然后几天后，来自新墨西哥州的民主党人汤姆·尤德尔也发表了他的告别演说，说了同样的话，关于这个机构是多么破败。

sentences.en: The Senate is broken.
sentences.zh: 参议院瘫痪了。

sentences.en: The Senate is broken.
sentences.zh: 参议院瘫痪了。

sentences.en: And it's not working for the American people.
sentences.zh: 它没有为美国人民服务。

sentences.en: We are becoming better and better political warriors.
sentences.zh: 我们正变得越来越擅长政治斗争。

sentences.en: Our peacemaking skills are atrophying.
sentences.zh: 我们的和平缔造技能正在萎缩。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, the structures we have built reward us for hurting one another.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，我们建立的结构奖励我们互相伤害。

sentences.en: We need to reform those structures or we'll never make progress.
sentences.zh: 我们需要改革这些结构，否则我们永远无法取得进展。

sentences.en: But the conclusion he drew was completely opposite.
sentences.zh: 但他得出的结论却截然相反。

sentences.en: He said it was time to get rid of the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 他说现在是时候废除阻挠议事规则了。

sentences.en: I've proposed Senate rules changes to make sure this institution does not remain a graveyard for progress.
sentences.zh: 我已经提议修改参议院规则，以确保这个机构不会继续成为进步的坟墓。

sentences.en: The promise of the filibuster is that the majority will find common ground with the minority.
sentences.zh: 阻挠议事规则的承诺是多数派会与少数派找到共同点。

sentences.en: But the reality of the filibuster is paralysis, a deep paralysis.
sentences.zh: 但阻挠议事的现实是瘫痪，一种深度的瘫痪。

sentences.en: Nothing important, nothing that really needed to happen was going to get done.
sentences.zh: 没有什么重要的事情，没有什么真正需要发生的事情能够完成。

sentences.en: And so that is kind of the fundamental tension that we're seeing play out right now.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们现在看到的正在上演的基本张力。

sentences.en: You have a new president who has said he wants to get big things done, but he's also said he wants unity and bipartisanship.
sentences.zh: 你有一位新总统，他说他想完成大事，但他也说他想要团结和两党合作。

sentences.en: And those two things may be at odds and we'll just have to see whether they are.
sentences.zh: 这两件事可能存在矛盾，我们只能拭目以待。

sentences.en: And the fate of the filibuster is pretty much going to turn on the answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 阻挠议事规则的命运很大程度上将取决于那个问题的答案。

sentences.en: Thank you, Julie.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，朱莉。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: In my view, we've already waited too long to deal with this climate crisis.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，我们处理这场气候危机已经等待太久了。

sentences.en: We can't wait any longer.
sentences.zh: 我们不能再等了。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, President Biden signed a series of sweeping executive orders designed to confront climate change.
sentences.zh: 周三，拜登总统签署了一系列旨在应对气候变化的全面行政命令。

sentences.en: Among other things, the orders require federal agencies to end subsidies for fossil fuels, stop issuing federal oil and gas leases,
sentences.zh: 除其他事项外，这些命令要求联邦机构停止对化石燃料的补贴，停止发放联邦石油和天然气租约，

sentences.en: and reserve 30 percent of all federal land and water for conservation by 2030.
sentences.zh: 并到2030年将所有联邦土地和水域的30%保留用于保护。

sentences.en: And we see it with our own eyes, we feel it, we know it in our bones, and it's time to act.
sentences.zh: 我们亲眼所见，我们亲身感受，我们骨子里知道，现在是采取行动的时候了。

sentences.en: And Britain will now require that citizens returning from 22 different countries quarantine in hotels for 10 days to avoid spreading variants of the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 英国现在将要求从22个不同国家返回的公民在酒店隔离10天，以避免传播新冠病毒的变种。

sentences.en: It is the kind of requirement that many public health experts believe that the United States should institute
sentences.zh: 这是许多公共卫生专家认为美国应该采取的要求，

sentences.en: to keep American travelers from bringing new, more contagious strains of the virus back into the country.
sentences.zh: 以防止美国旅客将新的、传染性更强的病毒株带回国内。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Sydney Harper, Rachel Quester, Robert Jemison, and Alexandra Lee Young.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由悉尼·哈珀、雷切尔·奎斯特、罗伯特·杰米森和亚历山德拉·李·杨制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周编辑，克里斯·伍德担任工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期接待做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或任何你喜欢收听的地方收听《Wirecutter秀》。
